evidence.section: 2.1. Preparation of Materials and Laser Welding
evidence.quote: The bulk HEA specimen was prepared by casting into a graphite mold with a cavity of 140 (L) × 30 (W) × 28 mm (H).

evidence.section: 2.1. Preparation of Materials and Laser Welding
evidence.quote: The as-cast HEA was homogenized at 1100 ◦C for 24 h

evidence.quote: and then quenched with water

evidence.section: 2.1. Preparation of Materials and Laser Welding

evidence.section: 2.1. Preparation of Materials and Laser Welding
evidence.quote: and finally was annealed at 800 ◦C for 1 h

evidence.section: 2.1. Preparation of Materials and Laser Welding
evidence.quote: the base, FeCoNiCrMn HEA, was laser-welded with preplaced FeCoNiCrMn or FeCoNiCrAl powders
Clearly, the base and FeCoNiCrMn powder are of a single FCC structure
the base and FeCoNiCrMn powder are of a single FCC structure and the FeCoNiCrAl powder shows a single BCC structure

the base has a single phase with cellular grains

mechanisms.name: grain growth perpendicular to solid/liquid interface

evidence.quote: the growth of grains in the fusion zone usually is initiated at the fusion line (Figure 4), and the grains tend to grow in the direction perpendicular to the solid/liquid interface due to the maximum temperature gradient and heterogenous nucleation
laser beam processing generally produces a rapid cooling rate which can promote the refinement of grains in the cast microstructure
the loss of the Mn element in the weld can be attributed to its low saturated vapor pressure

mechanisms.name: crack weakening of plastic deformation stability

evidence.quote: the fusion line of W3 consists of some cracks and this case has not taken place in W1 and W2. This case strongly weakens the stability of plastic deformation.
The main reason for this case may be the higher wettability of the same composition than different compositions.
